$comment: Slate's own defaults that every format shares: the pace ceiling, caption limits, loudness presets, the default budgets from plan §8, the two channel routes and the format aliases. A format file states its own values; slate.formats checks them against these (a format may be tighter, never looser). Edit here, then run `slate formats check`.

pace.source: Plan §7, stage 3: voice-over at no more than 2.6 words per second of shot.

sources.title: Slate plan, Quality: accessibility gate
sources.says: Captions at no more than 17 characters a second, and 2 lines of 42.

sources.title: Nimdzi: Subtitling vertical videos, guidelines where art thou? (2019-11-17)
sources.says: The BBC caps lines at 37 characters; Netflix's vertical previews run 33 characters a line without hurting readability; one or two lines; each caption 1 to 6 seconds. No platform sets a vertical standard, so Slate uses 32 for 9:16 and 36 for square and 4:5.

web.standard: Slate's delivery target for web, social and streaming (plan §7, stage 9: -14 LUFS +/-0.5, no louder than -1 dBTP)

ebu_r128.standard: EBU R 128 (Europe and most of the world)

sources.title: EBU R 128
sources.says: -23 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP maximum true peak, +/-0.5 LU.

sources.title: ProVideo Coalition: The CALM Act and commercial loudness
sources.says: ATSC A/85: -24 LKFS integrated, +/-2 dB, with true peaks no higher than -2 dBTP (a secondary source; check the broadcaster's own delivery spec).

reel_or_ad.label: Reel or ad (6-45 s)
reel_or_ad.note: Generation only when it's allowed and adds something. About 1% of a Pro month.

explainer.label: Explainer (60-120 s)
explainer.note: 0-2 generated shots at about $15-30 each, including one reject.

brand_film.label: Brand film (2-6 min)
brand_film.note: What the first brand films spent; the voice-over range includes tag A/B takes.

onboarding.label: Brand onboarding (once per brand)
onboarding.note: Voice Design about 5,000 credits and $15-20 of look tests; the sound reference is made locally.

budgets.source: Plan §8, Default budgets (2026-09-30): a hard stop at the budget, up to 1.5x for rework; prices live in registry.json with the date they were checked.

hero.label: Hero placement
hero.how: A derived film (slate variant <film> <child> --aspect <aspect> --format <format>) through the whole pipeline.
hero.master: After Effects finishes films a person supervises, started by that person; ffmpeg masters autonomous and draft films, which are held.

social.label: Social cut-down
social.how: A derived film rendered with fewer motion-blur samples and mastered with ffmpeg, so a cut-down takes minutes, not an evening.
social.gates: Every film gate still runs; a derived film never inherits its parent's results.

candidate.rule: Kept as the fast route only if the phase 8 benchmark shows it is genuinely faster than a Remotion cut-down at acceptable quality (decision 9).

broadcast.rule: Film, TV and radio need an Eleven Music Enterprise licence; online commercial use is fine on paid plans. A format or film.json with broadcast: true makes the sound module's music-licence gate ask for that licence.
broadcast.loudness: Use the broadcaster's standard (EBU R 128 or ATSC A/85) instead of the web target.
broadcast.source: Plan, Risks and licences: Eleven Music terms (2026-09-30).
